chunks: Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shuʿayb al-Haddad, from Zurays al-Kunasi, who said:
I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, and Abu Basir was with him. So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said:

Indeed, Dawud inherited the knowledge of the Prophets, and indeed Sulayman inherited Dawud, and indeed Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم inherited Sulayman, and indeed we inherited Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and indeed with us are the scriptures of Ibrahim and the tablets of Musa.
So Abu Basir said, “Surely this is the knowledge.” He said, “O Abu Muhammad, this is not the knowledge. Rather, knowledge is that which occurs in the night and the day, day by day and hour by hour.”

key_terms.أَلْوَاحَ: tablets; here, the tablets of Musa عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the Prophets; the bearers of revealed knowledge before the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: by the night; part of the expression for ongoing temporal recurrence
key_terms.بِسَاعَةٍ: hour by hour; indicating constant and renewed disclosure
key_terms.صُحُفَ: scriptures or parchments; here, the scriptures of Ibrahim عليه السلام
key_terms.عِلْمَ: knowledge; here, divinely granted knowledge of the Prophets
key_terms.وَرِثَ: inherited; refers to the transmission of prophetic knowledge
key_terms.يَحْدُثُ: occurs or comes to pass; indicating continuously renewed knowledge

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe the inherited knowledge of the Prophets and the ongoing nature of divine knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the knowledge of the Prophets passed in inheritance through Dawud, Sulayman, and the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and then to the Imams عليهم السلام. It further clarifies that true divinely granted knowledge is not limited to inherited scriptures and tablets, but includes continually renewed knowledge disclosed night and day.
